questions.1_who_assigned: Competition platforms and their problem setters. LiveCodeBench re-buckets, it does not estimate.
questions.2_when_assigned: At or before contest publication; LeetCode's label and AtCoder point values exist when the problem is released, CodeForces ratings shortly after.
questions.3_inputs: LeetCode native Easy/Medium/Hard; AtCoder setter point values; CodeForces problem ratings.
questions.8_agent_would_reasonably_have_it: Yes for benchmark evaluation -- it ships in the problem record. NOT guaranteed for a novel problem in deployment; see limitations.
questions.9_stable_across_releases: UNVERIFIED. Internally consistent within the cached snapshot (0 question_ids with conflicting difficulty). Stability across releases v1..v6 was not tested.
questions.10_official_field: Official LiveCodeBench dataset field, not derived experiment metadata.

paper.leetcode: The platform also provides a difficulty label for each problem which we use to tag the problems as Easy, Medium, and Hard.
paper.atcoder: The problems are assigned numeric difficulty ratings, and we exclude abc problems with a rating of more than 500. We also use these numeric ratings to tag the problems as Easy, Medium, and Hard.
paper.codeforces: CodeForces also provides difficulty ratings for the problems which we use to tag the problems as Easy, Medium, and Hard using the rating brackets {800}, (800-1000], and (1000-1300] respectively.

runner_code.finding: Difficulty is an Enum(easy/medium/hard) and __post_init__ only does Difficulty(self.difficulty) -- the runner READS the field, it never computes it. Dataset-construction/scraping code is not in the public repo (lcb_runner only).

empirical_atcoder.test: Does difficulty track the AtCoder problem letter, which proxies setter point value?
empirical_atcoder.conclusion: Monotone in letter; only b and d straddle a boundary, which is what varying per-contest point values produce. Rules OUT kenkoooo/AtCoderProblems solve-rate difficulty, whose scale runs to ~4000 and would be almost entirely excluded by the paper's 500 cutoff.

schema.finding: No solve rate, pass rate, submission count or model result anywhere in the record. `metadata` contains only func_name, for LeetCode's functional harness.

caveats.issue: CodeForces ratings are computed from HUMAN contestant performance after the contest.
caveats.why_acceptable: Human, not model; independent of LiveCodeBench's hidden tests and of any LLM evaluation. It is outcome-derived at one remove, from a different population.
caveats.exposure: 9 of 475 problems in the E0029 split (1.9%)

caveats.why_acceptable: Any experiment must pin the dataset snapshot, which the grading stage already records by sha256 per shard.

A Governor relying on difficulty needs that metadata at decision time. True for benchmark evaluation; not guaranteed for a novel problem in production. Any claim built on it is contingent on the metadata existing.

decision: ADMISSIBLE. Per the E0030 decision rule, CONTEST_RATING_DERIVED permits designing a new preregistered experiment around it.
